title: The 1946 line-up with Paul Gonsalves
summary: With Jo and Walter back, Dance reads the band; Greene says Gonsalves worked out beautifully.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, how long was the nucleus of that band like that, Stan?
Well, in '46 you've got Jo Jones and Walter Page back.
Oh, yeah.
Mm hmm.
Well, that must have been -- that's -- in other words that's --
Well, what happened to Walter Page when he went --
I don't know where he went.
I wonder was he sick during that period and came back? I wonder what happened. I'm lost -- during that period.
Yeah. But, in '46 Walter Page and Jo Jones were back.
Paul Gonsalves was in the band.
Well, Stanley, so -- once Walter Page and Jo Jones were back -- read us off the line-up of the band there, will you?
Ed Lewis, Harry Edison, Snooky Young, Emmett Berry. Bill Johnson -- trombone.
Trombone -- from Detroit.
Oh. Ted Donelly, George Matthews, Eli Robinson.
Mm hmm.
Preston Love, Rudy Rutherford, Buddy Tate, Paul Gonsalves, -- Jack Washington is back. So, he must have gotten drafted.
Well, so, Illinois is gone. Huh?
Yeah.
Yeah.
Paul is here.
Paul and Buddy are the two guys.
Paul Gonsalves. Yeah. Him, too.
Well, Paul wasn't in it very long, was he?
Well, he was there a year or two --
Yeah. He was there -- maybe -- a couple of years.
How did that work out?
Oh, it worked out beautifully.
Did it?
Yeah.
He was sort of in good shape in those days.
Yeah. Yeah. He was, and he wasn't drinking, and you know -- he was in good shape. His playing was wonderful.
